title: Torsion en cohomologie cristalline : notes manuscrites (s.d.), copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: Setting (§8.5, crystalline torsion notes, probably mid-1960s: the text still waits for 'fondements satisfaisants pour la cohomologie cristalline'). X is smooth projective of dimension n over k of characteristic p, polarized in P^r. Y = X ∩ H is a smooth hypersurface section of degree d, of dimension n-1. E(Y) is the 'new' (vanishing/primitive) part of the crystalline H^{n-1}(Y), as a W-module with Frobenius. E(Y,O_Y) is its coherent analogue built from H^{n-1}(Y,O_Y). The index ss means the semisimple part for the p-linear Frobenius, i.e. the part where F is bijective. By Artin–Schreier/Lang it is H^{n-1}_et(Ybar, F_p)⊗k, the 'Hasse–Witt part in the critical dimension'. (8.5.1) is an exact sequence containing the fundamental homomorphism φ: E(Y)⊗k → E(Y,O_Y)_ss. Over k this is the comparison 'unit-root part of crystalline cohomology mod p' → 'F-stable part of coherent cohomology'. The previous page did two things. First, it assembled these sequences, for Y varying in the open set U_d of the space of degree-d hypersurfaces (smooth section, E(Y,O_Y)_ss of maximal rank), into an exact sequence of locally free O_{U_d}-modules with semisimple p-linear operator. Equivalently (8.4.2) these are étale F_p-local systems, i.e. F_p-representations of G = π1(U_d). Second, it showed ker φ is a constant local system coming from H^n(X,O_X)_ss. On this page, for k finite and after a finite extension making Frobenius act with eigenvalues 1 on that constant part, Grothendieck concludes the following. The mod-p Frobenius eigenvalues on E(Y), for Y over a closed point of U_d, are completely governed by one finite-dimensional F_p-representation of G: the monodromy of the Hasse–Witt local system E(Y,O_Y)_ss. They are governed together with the (Chebotarev) distribution of Frobenius elements in G as the point varies. Mod p, the non-unit eigenvalues reduce to 0, so the characteristic polynomial of Frobenius mod p is that of the unit-root part. 8.5.10 (as corrected by hand) states: φ is injective, hence bijective, iff w (a map in the long exact sequence of the pair X, Y, from 8.5.1/8.5.7) is surjective, i.e. iff (pTors^n(X))_ss = 0. The 'only if' holds under the reservation Ker v = 0 of 8.5.7. A sufficient condition is that X has no p-torsion in crystalline H^n, equivalently by duality none in H^{n+1} (Tors H^i is dual to Tors H^{2n+1-i}). If X lifts with its polarization to characteristic 0, this sufficient condition 'should be expressible' through the analogous condition on torsion in the p-adic (étale or singular) cohomology of the lifted variety. The struck passage records an initial plan: rewrite (8.5.3) for the lift tensored by Z/p and ask that w_p be surjective or injective. It also records a belief that even for n=2, φ can fail to be surjective, so that the correction term dim Ker w or t^{n-1}(X,p) in inequality (8.5.6) cannot be dropped. The next page replaces this with Serre's Mexico example: a free Z/p quotient of a complete intersection, cut down to a surface, makes φ non-injective. It also gives a Künneth construction X×Z for non-surjectivity when n≥4. The purpose of the whole section is to show that sections Y of large degree have E(Y) of maximal Hodge level n-1 (nonzero unit-root part, 'ordinary in the critical dimension'), and to control how far crystalline torsion obstructs this.
errors: The setting allows k 'not even perfect', which is delicate for crystalline cohomology with W(k) coefficients. This is a foundational gap rather than an error, and Grothendieck himself flags that foundations are missing.

The equivalence/translation of the crystalline torsion condition into torsion of the p-adic cohomology of a lift is stated as expectation. In full generality, crystalline torsion of the special fibre can strictly exceed étale torsion of the generic fibre (Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze). Only the direction 'no crystalline torsion ⇒ no étale torsion of the lift' holds. The hand-inserted word 'suffisante' partly hedges this, but a translation in terms of the lift is only safe in one direction, or for the ss/unit-root part under extra hypotheses.

The struck guess that φ can fail to be surjective already for n=2 is not substantiated on this page. The next page instead produces non-injectivity for surfaces, and non-surjectivity only for n≥4 via Künneth, with n=3 left open. This is consistent with Grothendieck abandoning the passage.

'Description complète de la variation des valeurs propres mod p': this is accurate only for the reduction mod p of the characteristic polynomial, i.e. the unit roots mod p. It says nothing about p-adic unit roots beyond mod p.

ideas.what: Equivalence between locally free modules with a bijective (semisimple) p-linear Frobenius and étale F_p-local systems, i.e. F_p-representations of π1. Applied to the Hasse–Witt part of a family of hypersurface sections.
ideas.modern_name: Lang/Katz correspondence between unit-root F-modules and étale F_p- (later Z_p-) local systems; mod-p Riemann–Hilbert in the étale setting
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lang; Katz (SGA 7 exp. XXII; 'p-adic properties of modular schemes', 1973, Prop. 4.1.1)
ideas.where_published: Implicit in SGA 4½/SGA 7 circles (Katz's expositions); Grothendieck's own role unsure

ideas.what: Mod-p Frobenius eigenvalues on the vanishing crystalline cohomology of hypersurface sections Y are governed by the monodromy representation of π1(U_d) on the Hasse–Witt local system, plus the Chebotarev distribution of Frobenius elements.
ideas.modern_name: Mod-p monodromy of the unit-root (ordinary) part of a family; equidistribution of Hasse–Witt matrices; mod-p shadow of Dwork's unit-root zeta function
ideas.usually_credited_to: Igusa (monodromy of Hasse invariant, elliptic curves); Katz (p-adic monodromy, unit-root F-crystals, 1970s); Ekedahl (1987, mod-p monodromy for curves); Dwork/Wan (unit-root L-functions)
ideas.where_published: not in Grothendieck's published texts as far as known

ideas.what: Criterion: the comparison map φ from crystalline (unit-root part mod p) to the F-stable coherent cohomology of the section Y is bijective iff the semisimple p-torsion of crystalline H^n(X) vanishes. Sufficient: no p-torsion in H^n, or dually H^{n+1}.
ideas.modern_name: Control of the Hasse–Witt/Newton behaviour of hyperplane sections by crystalline torsion (Lefschetz-type statement for slope-0 parts); relation between torsion and the slope spectral sequence/de Rham–Witt
ideas.usually_credited_to: Illusie (de Rham–Witt complex, 1979) and Illusie–Raynaud for torsion analysis; Lefschetz-type statements for crystalline cohomology (Berthelot, Ogus)

ideas.what: Expectation that crystalline torsion of a liftable X matches torsion in the p-adic étale or singular cohomology of the lift.
ideas.modern_name: Comparison of torsion between crystalline cohomology of the special fibre and étale cohomology of the generic fibre (integral p-adic Hodge theory)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Fontaine–Messing, Faltings, Caruso (small ranges); Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze 2018 (general inequality and counterexamples)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck's 'problème de la fonction mystérieuse' (1970 ICM talk, Groupes de Barsotti–Tate) concerns comparison but not this torsion statement explicitly

ideas.what: Use of a free Z/p quotient of a complete intersection (Serre's Mexico 1956 example), plus Künneth products, to show the correction terms are necessary (next page).
ideas.modern_name: Serre's example of non-liftable/torsion phenomena; Künneth in crystalline cohomology

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly frames the variation, over the parameter space of hypersurface sections, of Frobenius eigenvalues mod p on the unit-root part as a monodromy-plus-Chebotarev problem for a single F_p-representation of π1(U_d), the 'Hasse–Witt local system'. This is an early mod-p version of the later programme of Katz (p-adic monodromy of unit-root crystals) and Dwork–Wan (unit-root L-functions). Here it is applied to arbitrary families of hyperplane/hypersurface sections of a fixed X, rather than modular or curve families.
missed.quote: On trouve alors une description complète de la variation des valeurs propres mod p de frobenius opérant sur E(Y), pour Y variable avec un point de U_d, en termes essentiellement de la seule représentation de G dans un vectoriel de dimension finie sur F_p, correspondant aux E(Y,O_Y)_ss
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The mod-p monodromy group of the Hasse–Witt local system of the universal hypersurface section of a given X is rarely computed (results exist mainly for curves, Ekedahl–Achter–Pries, and abelian varieties). Grothendieck's framing poses that computation, together with the equidistribution of Hasse–Witt matrices of sections, as the natural question.

missed.claim: The precise relation between the ss-part of crystalline p-torsion of X and the p-torsion of the cohomology of a characteristic-0 lift is left as 'doit pouvoir s'exprimer'. With the ss/unit-root restriction it may hold in a sharper form than the general BMS inequality.
missed.quote: cette condition, suffisante, doit aussi pouvoir s'exprimer ... par la condition analogue sur la torsion de cohomologie p-adique de la variété relevée
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Whether the unit-root (slope-0) part of crystalline torsion is detected by étale torsion of a lift is a concrete question in integral p-adic Hodge theory, related to BMS-type examples. It may have a clean answer via the étale Z_p-cohomology of the special fibre.

missed.claim: Existence of examples with n=3 where φ is not surjective is left open (next page: 'Il y a sans doute aussi des exemples avec n=3').
missed.quote: Je pense que même si n= dimX = 2, il peut arriver que φ ne soit pas surjectif
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor open example question about the crystalline torsion of threefolds controlling ordinarity of their surface sections. It is probably easy to settle with modern examples, e.g. Enriques-type or Godeaux-type quotients.

deep.surprise_reason: A thoughtful but mostly anticipatory page. It contains an early, explicit mod-p monodromy/Chebotarev framing of the Hasse–Witt variation in families of hypersurface sections, and a torsion criterion linking crystalline torsion of X to the ordinarity of its sections. These ideas were developed later by others (Katz, Illusie, BMS). The specific torsion criterion for sections does not seem to appear in the literature in this form, but it is a technical lemma rather than a major missed result.
transcription_corrections: Handwritten insertion above 'si et seulement si' reads 'donc bijectif', so the statement becomes 'est injectif, donc bijectif, si et seulement si'.
The struck-through words before 'éléments de frobenius' are a typed 'frobenius' crossed out (rendered 'xxobenius' in the typescript).
Marginal insertion after 'surjectif' appears to read 'et il en est de même si (pTors^n(X))_{ss}=0' or similar; the reference is to the ss-part of the p-torsion of crystalline H^n.

'en dimension n' (typed n followed by a blotted digit) together with '(ou ce qui revient au même par dualité, en dimension n+1)'. This is consistent with torsion duality Tors^i ↔ Tors^{2n+1-i}; the corrected hand digits should read n and n+1.
'ce[s] [suffisantes] condition[s] ... doi[vent]' was hand-corrected to singular: 'cette condition, suffisante, doit'.
'les conditions analogues sur la cohomologie' was corrected to 'la condition analogue sur la torsion de la cohomologie p-adique'.
The final paragraph 'Je pense que même si n = dim X = 2 ...' is struck through, together with the preceding sentence on w_p (big zigzag deletion).
